hints: Start by picturing butanone clearly, it is the ketone $\text{CH}_3\text{COCH}_2\text{CH}_3$, not an alcohol or an aldehyde.
Remember how ketones behave: they resist oxidation by Tollens, and they are attacked by nucleophiles like $\text{CN}^-$ and hydride $\text{H}^-$.
Focus on the reduction product with $\text{NaBH}_4$, draw $\text{CH}_3\text{CH(OH)CH}_2\text{CH}_3$ and check if its central carbon has four different groups.
walkthrough:
**Identify what butanone is**

Think of butanone as a 4-carbon ketone. Its structure is $\text{CH}_3\text{COCH}_2\text{CH}_3$ with the $\text{C=O}$ in the middle.

This one fact rules out a lot. Only alcohols dehydrate, and only aldehydes give Tollens.

**Recall the two key nucleophilic additions**

The carbonyl carbon is electron-poor, so it is attacked by nucleophiles, not electrophiles.

$$\text{CH}_3\text{COCH}_2\text{CH}_3 + \text{HCN} \rightarrow \text{cyanohydrin by nucleophilic addition}$$
$$\text{CH}_3\text{COCH}_2\text{CH}_3 + [H] \text{ from NaBH}_4 \rightarrow \text{CH}_3\text{CH(OH)CH}_2\text{CH}_3$$

**Check chirality of the reduction product**

The product is butan-2-ol, $\text{CH}_3\text{CH(OH)CH}_2\text{CH}_3$. Look at carbon 2.

It is bonded to $\text{H}$, $\text{OH}$, $\text{CH}_3$ and $\text{CH}_2\text{CH}_3$. Four different groups means it is a chiral centre, so a chiral (racemic) product forms.

options.A: Incorrect. Dehydration with concentrated $\text{H}_2\text{SO}_4$ is a reaction of alcohols, not ketones. Butanone has no $\text{OH}$ to lose as water, so it cannot form $\text{CH}_2=\text{CHCH}=\text{CH}_2$ this way.
options.B: Incorrect. Tollens reagent oxidises aldehydes to carboxylic acids to give a silver mirror, but ketones like butanone are resistant to oxidation and give a negative result. Students often confuse aldehydes and ketones here.
options.C: Incorrect. Addition of HCN to a carbonyl is nucleophilic addition, not electrophilic addition. The nucleophile $\text{CN}^-$ attacks the slightly positive carbonyl carbon. The word electrophilic is the trap.
options.D: Correct. $\text{NaBH}_4$ reduces the ketone to the secondary alcohol butan-2-ol, $\text{CH}_3\text{CH(OH)CH}_2\text{CH}_3$. Carbon 2 is attached to four different groups, so it is chiral and the product is formed as a racemic mixture.
